citations.narrative:
A shelter structure within the enclosure housing 2 female pigs is in disrepair and does not protect the animals from injury.
There was an approximately 4-5inch long board hanging loosely by a single nail along the top to the entrance To the left
of the entrance way, the corner trim has broken off at the bottom and has left a sharp point. Additionally, the bottom
corners and the bottom sides of the doorway of the shelter also have worn and splintered wood.
Broken or worn shelter structures with sharp points, splintered wood, or broken hanging pieces in areas where animals
my come in contact can can lead to injury.
Indoor and outdoor housing facilities for the animals shall be structurally sound and shall be maintained in good repair to
protect the animals from injury.
To be corrected by September 30, 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representatives.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
